_about: Manual checks of incident-learning records against their original public source. Statuses: VERIFIED (all key claims match), PARTIAL (source reached, some claims differ or are absent), SOURCE_UNREACHABLE (original not retrievable; nothing filled in from guesswork). Only what the source page states is recorded as confirmed.

confirmed: Shinhan Bank breach affecting about 25,000 customers (Shinhan disclosed 2026-10-01)
Shinhan: personal and credit / loan-application information leaked
KB Kookmin Bank customer information exposed via an internal employee mobile system
discrepancies: record says KB Kookmin leaked data of 119 customers; source says about 100
record says an 'AI-powered penetration-testing tool' was found; source says only 'a cyberattack involving an artificial intelligence (AI) agent' (Shinhan)
intrusion date not stated in source

WAIO-INTEL-2026-003.corroboration_search: Other outlets (Reuters syndications via SecurityWeek, Security Affairs, Cybernews) report: the FBI removed a contractor over an unapplied patch on a third-party-managed platform; Reuters sources name Oracle PeopleSoft and Accenture; ShinyHunters claimed the breach. Not re-read here at the page level.
discrepancies: record states CVE-2026-35273 was exploited via a URL-encoding WAF bypass; corroborating reports say neither the FBI nor Reuters confirmed which flaw was used
record names FBIJobs.gov; not confirmed by the corroborating reports seen

confirmed: unauthorised persons compromised DTU profiles and used them to access DTUBasen (identity and access management)
up to 200,000 current and former users may be affected
CPR numbers, full names, home addresses among potentially affected data
DTU warns the data could make phishing and other fraud more convincing
discrepancies: record says 'stolen credentials'; source says only 'compromising DTU profiles' (method not stated)
record says contained 'the same day'; source says contained, with no date
attack date not stated in source

confirmed: a poorly crafted prompt to a generative AI tool writing marketing-email code exposed over 95,000 customer email addresses
described as human error in AI use, not tool malfunction
discrepancies: this is an accidental exposure, not an AI-enabled scam or impersonation (source mentions neither)
exposure occurred 'in April' (year not stated); 2026-09-30 is the incident-record date
regulator undertaking and the '999 other recipients' detail are not stated on this page
